paragraphs.title: The Future Ruler and Israel's Return

easy.explanation: The passage says that the ruler shall come forth from Bethlehem Ephratah.
easy.q: From what town shall the ruler come forth?

easy.explanation: The remnant of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel.
easy.q: What will happen to the remnant of his brethren?

easy.explanation: He shall stand and feed in the strength of the LORD.
easy.q: In whose strength shall the ruler lead?

medium.explanation: Bethlehem is described as little among the thousands of Judah.
medium.q: How is Bethlehem Ephratah described among the thousands of Judah?

answers: The ruler will lead them after they return
They will return only after the ruler falls
The ruler will leave them when they return
medium.explanation: After the appointed period, the remnant shall return, and the ruler shall shepherd them.
medium.q: What is the relationship between Israel's return and the ruler's leadership?

answers: An origin only from a distant country
medium.explanation: The phrase points to an origin reaching back to ancient times.
medium.q: What does the phrase “from of old, from everlasting” describe?

answers: A little place produces a ruler of great importance
A wealthy city produces a weak ruler
An enemy city produces a foreign king
challenge.explanation: Although Bethlehem is little, a significant ruler shall come forth from it.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between Bethlehem and the ruler?

answers: His influence will be limited to Judah
His greatness will reach far and wide
His influence will disappear after Israel returns
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that his greatness will extend to the ends of the earth.
challenge.q: What does “unto the ends of the earth” indicate about the ruler?

answers: Ancient origin, a period of waiting, Israel's return, and leadership in God's strength
War, idolatry, exile, and Israel's forgetfulness
Peace, fortress building, witchcraft, and Assyrian victory
challenge.explanation: These ideas follow the order presented in the passage.
challenge.q: Which sequence of ideas appears in the passage?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “this man shall be the peace.”
easy.q: What shall the ruler be according to the passage?

easy.explanation: The passage mentions the Assyrian coming into the land.
easy.q: Which nation may come into the land?

answers: Six shepherds and seven principal men
Seven shepherds and eight principal men
Eight shepherds and seven principal men
easy.explanation: The passage names seven shepherds and eight principal men.
easy.q: How many shepherds and principal men will be raised against Assyria?

answers: To lead the people into idolatry
medium.explanation: They will be raised when the Assyrian comes against the land.
medium.q: Why will the shepherds and principal men be raised up?

answers: They will surrender them to Assyria
They will waste them with the sword
They will rebuild them as fortresses
medium.explanation: They shall waste those lands with the sword.
medium.q: What will they do to the land of Assyria and the land of Nimrod?

medium.explanation: Principal men are people of authority and leadership.
medium.q: What does “principal men” mean in this passage?

answers: Peace is the promised condition, but defense is prepared if Assyria attacks
challenge.explanation: The passage presents peace while also describing protection from a possible attack.
challenge.q: How do peace and defense exist together in the passage?

answers: Israel will have organized leadership and strength against its enemy
challenge.explanation: The large number of leaders emphasizes organized strength against Assyria.
challenge.q: What may be understood from the seven shepherds and eight principal men?

answers: The action against Assyria will bring deliverance
Israel will be delivered only by surrendering
Assyria will deliver Israel while ruling it
challenge.explanation: The passage says that this action shall deliver them from the Assyrian.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the action against Assyria and deliverance?

paragraphs.title: The Remnant of Jacob Among the Nations

easy.explanation: The remnant of Jacob shall be in the midst of many people.
easy.q: Where shall the remnant of Jacob be?

answers: Dew and showers upon the grass
easy.explanation: The passage compares the remnant to dew and showers upon the grass.
easy.q: What is the remnant of Jacob compared to in the first image?

answers: A lion and a young lion
easy.explanation: The remnant is compared to a lion among the beasts and a young lion among the flocks.
easy.q: What is the remnant compared to among the nations?

answers: They tarry not for man or wait for the sons of men
medium.explanation: The passage emphasizes that they do not depend on human beings.
medium.q: What do the dew and showers have in common in this comparison?

medium.explanation: The lion imagery portrays strength that enemies cannot easily overcome.
medium.q: What does the image of the lion and young lion express?

medium.explanation: Showers are rains that refresh and nourish the grass.
medium.q: What are “showers” in the phrase “the showers upon the grass”?

answers: Refreshing influence together with independent strength
Weakness together with dependence on the nations
Isolation together with surrender of the land
challenge.explanation: The dew and showers suggest blessing, while the lion suggests strength and confidence.
challenge.q: Which combination of qualities describes the remnant of Jacob?

answers: It remains independent even while surrounded by many nations
It becomes completely absorbed into the nations
It depends on the nations to survive
challenge.explanation: The passage shows the remnant among the nations without dependence on them.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the remnant being among many people but not waiting for man?

answers: Its hand will be lifted up upon its adversaries, and its enemies will be cut off
It will ask its enemies for protection
challenge.explanation: The passage says that its hand will be lifted up upon its adversaries and its enemies cut off.
challenge.q: What will be the result of the remnant's strength?

paragraphs.title: The End of Military Power and Idolatry

easy.explanation: The LORD will cut off the horses and destroy the chariots.
easy.q: What will the LORD cut off from among the people?

answers: Cut off the cities and throw down the strong holds
easy.explanation: The passage says that the cities will be cut off and the strong holds thrown down.
easy.q: What will the LORD do to the cities and strong holds?

easy.explanation: The LORD will cut off the graven images and standing images.
easy.q: Which objects connected with idolatry will be cut off?

answers: They will no longer be needed
They will create peace by themselves
medium.explanation: The removal of these military powers shows that they will no longer be needed.
medium.q: Why will the horses, chariots, and strong holds be removed?

answers: Military power is removed, witchcraft and idols are removed, and vengeance is taken upon the heathen
Fortresses are built, armies are enlarged, and idols are accepted
Chariots are restored, images are erected, and Israel submits to Assyria
medium.explanation: This is the main progression of actions in the passage.
medium.q: What sequence of actions is described in the passage?

answers: People who practice divination or claim to foretell the future
medium.explanation: Soothsayers are people who practice forms of divination or fortune-telling.

answers: Both remove powers in which the people had trusted instead of the LORD
Both describe Israel's return to Bethlehem
challenge.explanation: The passage describes the removal of military and false spiritual powers.
challenge.q: What connection exists between removing military power and removing idols and witchcraft?

answers: The people will no longer worship images made by human hands
The people will worship their weapons
The people will serve the fortresses
challenge.explanation: The statement rejects worship of idols made by human beings.
challenge.q: What does “thou shalt no more worship the work of thine hands” mean?

answers: The heathen that have not heard the LORD
challenge.explanation: The LORD will execute vengeance upon the heathen who have not heard Him.
challenge.q: Against whom will vengeance be executed at the end of the passage?
